transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. I wanted to get us together to discuss the Atlas toolkit release scheduled for next Friday. As I understand it, the engineering team plans to publish it in our public repository, and it will include source code, documentation, and a sample training package for external developers. Before I can give my final legal approval, I need to make sure we've completed all the pre-release conditions across the board. Can I get updates from each of you on where things stand with the open-source, commercial, export-control, and privacy reviews for this release?

transcript.text: During my commercial review, I examined the largest customer's source-code agreement and found that the customer's proprietary connector is included in the current build of the Atlas toolkit. The agreement explicitly prohibits public release of that connector without written customer consent. This means the public package must exclude the connector, be limited to the core toolkit, and the exclusion must be documented in the release checklist. I have not yet added this contract restriction to the release checklist.
